module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 541

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/541](https://www.erdosproblems.com/541)
- [ErSz76] Erdős, E. and Szemerédi, E., On a problem of Graham. Publ. Math. Debrecen (1976),
  123--127.
- [GHW10] Gao, Weidong and Hamidoune, Yahya Ould and Wang, Guoqing, Distinct length modular zero-sum
  subsequences: a proof of Graham's conjecture. J. Number Theory (2010), 1425--1431.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos541

/--
Let $a_1, \dots, a_p$ be (not necessarily distinct) residues modulo a prime $p$, such that there
exists some $r$ so that if $S \subseteq [p]$ is non-empty and
$$\sum_{i \in S} a_i \equiv 0 \pmod{p}$$
then $|S| = r$.

Must there be at most two distinct residues amongst the $a_i$?

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle and ChatGPT.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos541.lean"]
theorem erdos_541 : answer(True) ↔ (∀ p, Fact p.Prime → ∀ (a : Fin p → ZMod p),
    (∃ r, ∀ (S : Finset (Fin p)), S ≠ ∅ → ∑ i ∈ S, a i = 0 → S.card = r) →
      (Set.range a).ncard ≤ 2) := by
  sorry

/-- Gao, Hamidoune, and Wang [GHW10] solved this for all moduli `p` (not necessarily prime). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_541.variants.general_moduli (p : ℕ) (a : Fin p → ZMod p)
    (ha₀ : ∃ r, ∀ (S : Finset (Fin p)), S ≠ ∅ → ∑ i ∈ S, a i = 0 → S.card = r) :
      (Set.range a).ncard ≤ 2 := by
  sorry

/-- This was proved by Erdős and Szemerédi [ErSz76] for p sufficiently large. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_541.variants.large_primes : ∀ᶠ p in atTop, p.Prime → ∀ a : Fin p → ZMod p,
    (∃ r, ∀ (S : Finset (Fin p)), S ≠ ∅ → ∑ i ∈ S, a i = 0 → S.card = r) →
      (Set.range a).ncard ≤ 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos541

findings.description: The [ErSz76] bibliography entry gives the first author as “Erdős, E.” rather than “Erdős, P.” This is only a bibliographic slip; it does not affect any mathematical statement.
findings.source_evidence: The Rényi Institute archive entry for 1976-18 lists “P. Erdős, E. Szemerédi: On a problem of Graham”. Gao–Hamidoune–Wang also identify these authors as “P. Erdős and E. Szemerédi” in reference [ES] of arXiv:0902.4758.
findings.suggested_fix: In the module bibliography, replace “Erdős, E.” with “Erdős, P.”

reformulations.difference: Gao–Hamidoune–Wang assume a positive modulus; Lean quantifies over every natural modulus, including zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive p, ZMod p represents exactly the residues in [0,p−1]. For p = 0, although ZMod 0 is ℤ, the sequence has domain Fin 0, so its range is empty and its ncard is 0. Thus the extra case is automatically true. The equivalence between the all-natural-moduli statement and its positive-moduli restriction was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the problem's sorry-backed theorems.

reformulations.difference: The original Erdős–Szemerédi formulation assumes nonzero residues, whereas Lean also permits zero residues.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The additional case is independently settled for every positive modulus. If a sequence satisfying the hypothesis contains zero, remove that occurrence. The remaining p−1 terms must be zero-sum-free: any nonempty zero-sum selection from them, with and without the removed zero, would give two different zero-sum lengths. The elementary lemma stated by Gao–Hamidoune–Wang says that a zero-sum-free sequence of length p−1 modulo p has at most one distinct value. Restoring zero therefore gives at most two values. Their proof explicitly makes this reduction. Consequently the nonzero-residue and unrestricted sufficiently-large-prime statements are equivalent.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalizations were found in the three theorems. The positive answer and all solved tags agree with the sources. Lean checks confirmed the inferred quantifiers, the ordinary threshold meaning of eventually atTop, and finiteness of every range. Independent scratch proofs established that the hypothesis is satisfiable for every modulus (the all-ones sequence) and is equivalent to the computable condition that nonempty zero-sum subsets have at most one distinct length. Exhaustive tests for moduli 1–5 found no counterexamples. The linked external theorem has exactly the main statement's right-hand side and contains no sorry or custom axioms in its source. Its original Lean 4.24 proof was not independently replayed: recompiling with the available Lean 4.33 environment encounters Mathlib API changes, which is not evidence of a mathematical or status defect.
